Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%88%D8%A8%D8%B1. The Academy defines الوَبَر as camel wool/rabbit fur and gives its plural أَوْبَار; it also records وَبِرَ with imperfect يَوْبَرُ and وَبَّرَ with several established lexical meanings.
The initial و is retained in the noun and in the imperfect يَوْبَرُ; the Qur’anic أَوْبَارِهَا is the plural noun with conjunction, genitive and possessive shell preserved only in the current row.
وَبْرٌ ‘hyrax’ was investigated but not selected: it is a separate lexical branch and the four accepted rows already teach the material noun and its verbal/derived development.
Article, conjunction وَ, case ending and possessive ـهَا were not counted.
وَبْرٌ: hyrax

مُواطَنَةٌ was investigated but not selected: although same-root and attested, its modern civic sense is less directly useful here than the classical place/verb family.

مَوْقِذٌ and وَقِيذٌ were investigated; they are attested, but the selected rows give a cleaner active/action/derived relationship to المَوْقُوذة.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%8A%D9%82%D8%B8. The Academy defines يَقِظَ with waking and alertness meanings, gives أَيْقَاظ as its plural, and records أَيْقَظَ, تَيَقَّظَ, استيقظَ and اليَقَظَة.

The initial ي is a radical in the lexical root ي ق ظ. The Qur’anic أَيْقَاظًا is the plural adjective ‘awake/alert’; it is not the Form-IV maṣdar أَيْقَاظًا, despite the identical surface spelling in unvocalised text.

يَقِظٌ was investigated but rejected as number-only padding relative to أَيْقَاظًا; the word’s identical unvocalised spelling with the Form-IV maṣdar was explicitly disambiguated by vocalisation and morphology.
Accusative plural ending was not counted.
يَقِظٌ: awake / alert

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%B9. The Academy defines يَنَعَ with imperfect يَيْنَعُ/يَيْنِعُ, maṣdars يَنْعًا and يُنْعًا, and the adjective يانِعٌ; it also records أَيْنَعَ as a derived form.

The initial ي is a root radical. The Qur’anic وَيَنْعِهِۦٓ is the ripening noun with conjunction, genitive and possessive shell; the root’s weak-initial behavior does not justify treating those shells as Ṣarf rows.
يَنْعٌ was investigated but not duplicated: it is the lexical noun underlying the current وَيَنْعِهِۦٓ, so its bare form would only remove conjunction, case and possessive shell.
The Academy’s alternate imperfect يَيْنِعُ is documented in evidence but not added as a separate row from يَيْنَعُ because the difference is vocalic variant within the same tense/stem.
يَنْعٌ: ripeness

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D9%88%D8%A8%D9%82.
